scope: search-only same-artifact native Linux experiment; separate from Rust-built lifecycle evidence

validation.warmup_note: full warmup asserted where row fields are present; Rust rows do not serialize the warmup count
validation.latency_summary: median of three per-repeat public-call percentiles; not a pooled percentile or confidence interval

ordered_result_parity.status: exact ordered ID and full-distance parity on every compared query and label
ordered_result_parity.interpretation: 6,000 comparisons reuse the same 2,000 queries at three breadths; they are not 6,000 independent queries

multihop_established_fixed_L64.qualification: fixed established baseline; final multihop L60 is faster and also meets the 95% floor

fastest_final_measured_multihop_at_95_fl.interpretation: common recall floor, not identical recall or a claim of globally optimal tuning

historical_inline_L320.status: historical frozen baseline; not refreshed in the final round at L320
historical_inline_L320.qualification: cross-round descriptive comparison; current final-round inline measurements at L60/64/144 all miss 95%

k1000_L4000.cpp_status: earlier retained baseline; unchanged C++ binary and matched workload/protocol, not a new same-round refresh
k1000_L4000.qualification: aggregate and every label's strict recall match C++; 256 unique queries, four per label, so tail and label estimates are coarse; recall is below 99%; one measured L, not a tuning optimum

limitations: read requests/bytes are logical reader requests, not physical SSD IOPS
same queries are reused for three timing repeats; deterministic repeated recall does not add independent quality samples
per-label tails use only the recorded small query samples and do not establish statistical significance
the shared graph was C++-built StitchedVamana; this summary does not measure a Rust-built graph or update lifecycle
